implemented: Immutable pipelines and source handles shared by worker/UI; short source-index locks; validation, upload and encoding outside the shared lock.
Immediate supported point edits from resident, validated, exact source crops; latest revision prevents stale worker replacement.
Fused vertical filter and SDR display conversion; unchanged canonical coefficients, fp32 operations and source precision; one RGBA32F intermediate removed.
Bounded source padding also used for settled pan refreshes; edits retain exact source crop admission.
Opt-in bounded CPU spans and asynchronous GPU timestamp readbacks; ordinary runtime has no diagnostic queries.

options_compared.option: Shorter locks and immediate resident point edits
options_compared.reason: Baseline upload keeps filter lock for milliseconds; point-edit worker encoding is submillisecond yet revision waits a UI cycle.

options_compared.option: Fuse vertical filtering with display conversion
options_compared.reason: Same per-pixel arithmetic, one less dispatch and full intermediate; verified against canonical CPU and retained separate GPU kernel.
Avoid repeated overlapping uploads within existing capability/byte quotas.
options_compared.tradeoff: Larger individual source uploads and residency. The paired pan traces transfer about 64 MB once instead of 124 MB across seven uploads; edit profiles including final canonical convergence transfer about 106 MB instead of 41 MB. This is not a reduction in every upload path.

options_compared.option: Pool all scratch/output resources and coefficient buffers
options_compared.reason: Measured resource setup is roughly 0.1 ms at this viewport; additional cross-frame lifetime management is not the main latency cost.

options_compared.option: Different workgroup sizes or GPU-generated coefficients
options_compared.reason: Small measured compute budget; changes require broader device and numerical qualification.

options_compared.option: Lower-detail input or resampling old display frame
options_compared.reason: Violates retained sharpness and canonical sampling requirements.

measurement_conditions.input_pacing: at least 16 ms, unchanged probe scheduling
measurement_conditions.viewport: approximately 855 x 596 backing pixels, edge snapping tolerance 1 px
measurement_conditions.window: ordinary native window, no forced size/position/topmost mode
measurement_conditions.ordering: before/after, after/before, before/after for GPU cases; before/after repeated three times for CPU control
measurement_conditions.during_gesture: no screenshots, surface readbacks or CPU reference rendering
measurement_conditions.profile_trials: separate from cadence trials, optional GPU queries and CPU spans enabled
measurement_conditions.decode: isolated copies and catalogs; native detail prepared before measured gesture; OS cache not flushed
measurement_conditions.statistics: median of three per-run percentile/max statistics; descriptive local results, not a confidence bound
measurement_conditions.small_geometry_exception: One baseline edit run recorded 854 rather than 855 px width; included within declared 1 px edge-snapping tolerance; original rejection retained.

observed_outcome.point_edit_latency: Median first draw of each revision falls from about 33.3 ms to 16.7 ms for both JPEG and Experimental RAW across three runs.
observed_outcome.zoom_pan_cadence: No uniform improvement: some visible interval/max statistics improve, others worsen; all runs and outliers are retained.
observed_outcome.pan_uploads: Seven uploads become one in each paired pan profile; transfer volume decreases from about 124 MB to 64 MB during the measured trace.
observed_outcome.intermediate_memory: At 855 x 596, fused vertical/display removes 8,153,264 bytes of scratch per encoded frame (full RGBA32F output minus 16-byte unused binding). This is not a claim about total process/GPU memory.

presentation_precision.scope: All pixels of generated grayscale/translucent ramps and extended/clipped alternating colors through production CPU/GPU presenter, at aligned 1:1 and nonintegral fit; native-format capture, SDR sRGB. Requested high-precision format must be reached. No physical display/link-depth, HDR, multi-monitor, Windows or statistical performance qualification.

validation.presentation_precision_scope: Eight CPU/GPU checks pass at 1:1 and fractional scale on BGRA8 and RGB10A2. Requested RGBA16Float surface is unavailable; the unmodified comprehensive probe reports false for those four unsupported-format cases.

limitations: Software draws and event-to-draw age are not physical display FPS or event-to-monitor latency.
GPU timestamps describe encoded passes. mapped_at_creation upload includes backend-managed transfers: allocation/copy/unmap CPU time is measured, GPU DMA duration is not isolated.
Submission-to-callback includes queue and polling scheduling, not pure GPU execution.
Timestamp precision/reordering and optional capability support are backend dependent.

GPU power states and clocks vary automatically even between adjacent trials. Early fast-clock profiles are retained as diagnostic evidence, not used for before/after speedup claims; paired profiles include read-only clock telemetry. No uniform GPU elapsed-time speedup is claimed.
Point-edit optimization does not extend to spatial effects, geometry, masks or active complex layers.
Memory pressure, missing source/LOD, larger viewports and other adapters can still delay frames.
Apple RAW and native macOS/XPC were not tested; no decoder/bundle changes and no R0-R4 or photographic gates closed.
RGBA16Float presentation surface is unavailable on this Windows adapter; RGB10A2 does exercise the fp16 intermediate. No physical panel/link-depth qualification.
Computer Use skill was read and retried; its node_repl runtime was not exposed. Native built-in probes provided the executed measurements.
